not_validated.item: Event times and visibility shares on real terrain
not_validated.reason: No independent illumination product or mission record has been compared yet. The terrain horizon has passed analytic tests of the core stream only (docs/method/horizon.md).

not_validated.item: Exact rise and set times at a real lander
not_validated.reason: No operator of the four missions examined published a sunrise or sunset clock time for its landing site. Operational records (hours of daylight, expected wake-up date) only bound the computed events from one side.

not_validated.item: Earth rise and set against an independent source
not_validated.reason: Horizons does not state which point of the Earth's disc its rise and set refer to; only the Earth's direction and size are validated.

not_validated.item: Eclipses of the Sun by the Earth
not_validated.reason: The visible fraction of the Sun does not include occultation by the Earth.

limits: Every check on this card except the Chandrayaan-3 bound is terrain-free. Near the lunar poles the terrain horizon, not the ephemeris, sets the accuracy of an event time: a horizon error of 0.01 deg can move an event by many minutes.
The external reference (Horizons) and the core use JPL ephemerides of the same family; an error common to both would not show.
Thresholds marked as written in the acceptance test were committed in the same commit as the code they test; only the Horizons thresholds have a commit of their own that predates the data.
